definition: Box-like device with a blade set in the top, used to shave a hard block of dried bonito into thin flakes.
Ceramic grinding bowl with fine ridges inside and a wooden pestle, used to grind sesame seeds and mash ingredients.
Grating dish with sharp ceramic tips and a ring around the bowl that collects juice, used on ginger, daikon and onion.
Lid set directly on top of food in a simmering pot to hold ingredients in place and spread heat evenly.
Wide shallow wooden tub for tossing freshly cooked rice with seasoning, absorbing moisture and cooling the rice quickly.
Flexible mat of bamboo strips used to shape and roll sushi and rolled omelet into tight cylinders.
Thin stainless saucepan with a pouring spout on each side and measuring marks inside, used for soups, stews and simmered food.
Lidded Japanese earthenware pot that holds heat well, used over a flame and then carried to the table for shared hot pots.
Chopping board of soft Japanese cypress wood that is gentle on knife edges, naturally fragrant and needs no oiling.
Carved wooden whisk twirled between the palms to froth hot chocolate and other hot drinks.
Slanted stone grinding slab worked with a hand stone, traditionally used to grind corn into dough and chiles into sauce.
Flat griddle of clay, aluminium or cast iron used to toast spices, blister chiles and cook or reheat tortillas.
Tall pot with a rack and lid for steaming tamales over simmering water.
Earthenware dish with a tall cone-shaped lid that returns condensed steam to the food, used for slow-cooked North African stews.
Flat, slightly concave metal pan that gives steady contact heat for cooking Indian flatbreads such as roti and dosa.
Curved blade moved with a rocking motion to mince herbs finely without bruising them.
Japanese-style weighted press that squeezes vegetables down while they pickle.
Compact single-flame gas burner set on the dining table to keep hot pots simmering or grill food while people eat.
Low wooden table frame with a heater underneath and a heavy blanket between frame and tabletop, used to keep the legs warm in winter.
Low Persian table with a heater beneath it and a thick cloth over it, around which people sit on the floor in winter.
Small tray-like wooden table from Korea, used for carrying food and as an individual dining table placed on the floor.
Woven rope-strung bed on four wooden legs from the Indian subcontinent, used for sleeping and sitting, especially in warm areas.
Backless couch or long cushioned seat traditionally used for reclining or lounging.
Glass-fronted display cabinet for showing collectibles, fine china or art while keeping them free of dust.
Tall standing unit with hooks, shelves and sometimes a bench, placed by an entrance to hold coats, hats and bags.
Free-standing rack with hangers and trays for laying out clothes, suits and accessories ready for the next day.
Seat hung from chains or ropes that sways back and forth, used outdoors on porches and verandas.
Long wooden bench with a backrest, traditionally found in churches or halls, seating several people in a row.
Desk with drawers on both sides and an open space in the middle for the user's legs.
Low, minimalist platform bed frame that sits close to the floor, inspired by Japanese interior style.
Soft seat filled with loose beads that moulds to the sitter's body, used for informal lounging.
Freestanding open shelving unit shaped like a leaning ladder, with tiers for holding books, plants or ornaments.
Thick quilt-like Japanese floor mattress of cotton wadding, laid on tatami at night and folded away into a closet by day.
Thick quilted Japanese bed cover laid over the sleeper, aired in the sun and used with a washable cover.
Quilt from South Asia with a cotton, silk or velvet cover stuffed with cotton wool, used for warmth in cold weather.
Handwoven thin flat rug from the Indian subcontinent, used as a floor covering or bed cover.
Small woven cotton mat about two feet square, laid on the floor to sit on during meditation.
Pileless tapestry-woven rug whose coloured weft threads form the whole design, used as a light portable floor covering or wall hanging.
Long narrow cylindrical pillow filled with down or feathers, used for decoration or to support the back against a headboard.
Small cylindrical pillow sewn closed, used to support the neck vertebrae or purely for decoration.
Decorative fabric panel that fits between mattress and box spring and hangs near the floor to hide the bed base and legs.
Decorative trimmed cover for a pillow, placed behind the pillows used for sleeping.
Countertop pot with a heating element, inner bowl and thermostat that boils or steams rice automatically.
Electric unit that pulls moisture out of room air to keep damp spaces such as basements free of mould.
Electric cabinet with trays and gentle warm airflow that dries fruit, vegetables and meat for preserving.
Small electric incubator with cups or a tub that holds milk at a steady warmth while it ferments.
Electric machine with a kettle and glass cabinet into which kernels and oil are poured to pop and serve popcorn.
Pair of hinged heated metal plates with a grid pattern that shut together to cook batter into waffles.
Hinged electric grill with two heated plates that presses and toasts sandwiches and vegetables.
Hand-held powered knife with twin reciprocating blades, used to carve roasts and slice delicate terrines or crusty bread.
Upright floor cleaner with a water tank on the handle that heats water and pushes steam through a pad.
Countertop appliance with a paddle and baking tin that kneads, proves and bakes a loaf from loose ingredients.
Refrigerated cabinet fitted with a tap and gas line that holds a keg of beer and serves it chilled on draught.
Table-top machine that stitches fabric together with thread, used to make new clothes or mend old ones.
Chisel with a hard steel front and soft steel back on the blade, used to shape and pare softwood.
Saw with a long coarse blade held taut in a bow-shaped frame, used to cut logs and branches roughly.
Fine saw with a stiff rib along the top edge of the blade, used for joinery, dovetails and cabinet work.
Wrench with an open jaw at one end and a tapered spike at the other, used to line up bolt holes in pipe flanges.
Small hand plane for trimming edges and end grain and making fine adjustments to woodwork.
Cranked hand tool that turns large drill bits by hand to bore holes, especially in timber.
Small hand tool with a screw-like tip that is twisted by hand to bore small holes in wood.
Handle that holds a threading die steady while it cuts external threads on rods or pipes.
Fluted hand tool that enlarges and finishes an existing hole to a more accurate size.
Cutter that makes a tapered recess around a hole so a screw head can sit flush with the surface.
Hand tool with coarse raised teeth that quickly shapes wood and other soft materials.
Stand-mounted drill that stays fixed while the work sits on an adjustable table for controlled, accurate drilling.
Garden hoe with a sharp, wide blade that skims just under the soil surface to slice weeds from their roots.
Loop-shaped garden hoe that pivots back and forth to cut stubborn weeds.
